title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented Hillsdale College traditions, from snow games and statue golf to senior sidewalk messages and ceremonial gatherings.

cards.title: Carry the Ball to Lady Thatcher
cards.subtitle: A snowy Quad game with an unusual goal line
cards.notes: Watch for the winter game on the Quad, where players score by carrying a football across the snow and placing it in Thatcher’s lap.
cards.short_summary: Hillsdale turns Margaret Thatcher’s Liberty Walk statue into the scoring target for a homegrown winter sport.
cards.evidence_claim: Hillsdale College describes Thatcherball as a winter sport invented and played at the College, with players scoring by dropping a football in the lap of Margaret Thatcher’s statue.
cards.access_notes: The College describes the game as a winter activity on the Quad; timing and participation details are not posted on the source page.

cards.title: Play the Liberty Walk as a Golf Course
cards.subtitle: Wiffle balls connect Hillsdale’s historic statues
cards.notes: Bring a nine iron and Wiffle ball only when the activity is organized, then follow the statue-to-statue route along Liberty Walk.
cards.short_summary: Students reinterpret Liberty Walk as a campus golf course whose landmarks serve as successive targets.
cards.evidence_claim: Hillsdale College documents Statue Golf as using a nine iron and Wiffle ball to play from statue to statue along Liberty Walk.
cards.access_notes: The official traditions page identifies Liberty Walk as the route but does not provide a current event schedule or participation rules.

cards.title: Dress Up for Dancing in the Arb
cards.subtitle: The semester’s first large Student Activities gathering
cards.notes: Look for the Student Activities Board announcement, then head to Slayton Arboretum for the themed evening of dancing and conversation.
cards.short_summary: Floral dress and outdoor dancing mark a campus gathering held near the start of Hillsdale’s fall semester.
cards.evidence_claim: Hillsdale College says Garden Party has been held since 2005 and is a Student Activities Board-sponsored dance in Slayton Arboretum early in the fall semester.
cards.source_title: Garden Party: The Event of the Season
cards.access_notes: The tradition is a campus Student Activities Board event; consult the current student calendar for that year’s date and attendance details.

cards.title: See Shakespeare Beneath the Trees
cards.subtitle: A student-led spring performance in Slayton Arboretum
cards.notes: Check the spring arts calendar before walking to the Arb; the troupe and its outdoor setting share the Shakespeare in the Arb name.
cards.short_summary: A student drama troupe stages the Bard outdoors in the same arboretum named by the group.
cards.evidence_claim: Hillsdale College reports that the student-led Shakespeare in the Arb troupe has performed Shakespeare plays in Slayton Arboretum each spring for more than a decade.
cards.access_notes: The official traditions page identifies a recurring spring performance but does not list current dates, admission terms, or weather arrangements.

cards.title: Leave a Blue-and-White Sidewalk Message
cards.subtitle: Graduating students mark campus paths at year’s end
cards.notes: During the senior-year activity, read the blue-and-white messages across campus paths and leave existing work undisturbed for others.
cards.short_summary: Hillsdale seniors close their college years by adding personal blue-and-white messages to campus sidewalks.
cards.evidence_claim: Hillsdale College says seniors earn the opportunity to finish their time on campus by painting blue-and-white messages on its sidewalk network.
cards.access_notes: The College presents this as a senior tradition; the source does not publish dates, materials guidance, or authorization procedures.

cards.title: Close the Academic Year at Centralhallapalooza
cards.subtitle: Hillsdale’s end-of-year campus festival
cards.notes: Follow Student Activities announcements near the end of the academic year for the festival lineup, location details, and attendance guidance.
cards.short_summary: Known on campus as CHP, the annual festival combines live entertainment with an end-of-year send-off.
cards.evidence_claim: Hillsdale College describes Centralhallapalooza as a large celebratory festival held at the end of the academic year with music acts and surprises.
cards.access_notes: The traditions page documents the end-of-year festival but does not provide a current date, performance lineup, or access policy.

cards.title: Hear Epic Poetry Read Across the Quad
cards.subtitle: Homer, Virgil, and Dante return to the outdoor stage
cards.notes: Pause at the small stage near the Quad during Epic Week and listen for the student readers’ rotating passages from major epic poems.
cards.short_summary: Two Hillsdale honor societies bring canonical epics into public view through an annual outdoor reading marathon.
cards.evidence_claim: Hillsdale College identifies Epic Week as an annual outdoor reading of epic poetry organized by Eta Sigma Phi and Lambda Iota Tau near the Quad.
cards.access_notes: The College documents an annual outdoor reading but does not post the current reading schedule or weather contingency on this page.

cards.title: Finish Homecoming with Mock Rock
cards.subtitle: Campus teams meet in a choreographed dance contest
cards.notes: Check the Homecoming schedule, then watch residence halls, Greek organizations, and independent teams present rehearsed group routines.
cards.short_summary: Hillsdale’s Homecoming competition culminates in a large student dance-and-performance contest.
cards.evidence_claim: Hillsdale College’s student-life calendar identifies Mock Rock as the final event of Homecoming Week, and College coverage documents it as an annual choreographed dance competition among campus teams.
cards.source_title: Mock Rock — Student Life at Hillsdale
cards.access_notes: The direct event page documents the September 27, 2025 edition; consult the current Homecoming calendar before planning attendance.

cards.title: Begin Hillsdale at Freshman Convocation
cards.subtitle: Incoming students gather with families and faculty
cards.notes: Incoming students should follow orientation instructions for the ceremony, which brings the new class, families, and faculty together.
cards.short_summary: A formal convocation opens the first-year experience with addresses, prayer, music, and shared campus commitments.
cards.evidence_claim: Hillsdale College’s 2025 announcement calls Freshman Convocation an orientation tradition and reports that incoming freshmen, families, and faculty attended the August 24 ceremony.
cards.source_title: Hillsdale College Welcomes Class of 2029 to Campus
cards.access_notes: The documented ceremony is intended for incoming freshmen and their families; participants should use their current orientation schedule.

cards.title: Gather at the Soldier Statue for Decoration Day
cards.subtitle: A historic campus observance revived in 2025
cards.notes: When the observance is scheduled, gather respectfully near the Soldier Statue for its historical address, hymns, and commemorative program.
cards.short_summary: Students revived a nineteenth-century Hillsdale remembrance ceremony honoring College soldiers and military service.
cards.evidence_claim: Hillsdale College reports that students revived Decoration Day in 2025 with a ceremony at the Soldier Statue featuring hymns, a historical address, a flag dedication, and a cannon salute.
cards.source_title: Hillsdale College Celebrates Veterans Day, Honors Those Who Served
cards.access_notes: The source documents a 2025 revival rather than guaranteeing an annual schedule; verify future observances through College announcements.

warnings: Decoration Day is documented as a tradition revived in 2025; the source does not establish that it will recur annually.
Current dates and participation rules were not available for several traditions, so no unverified scheduling or public-access claims were added.
